verdict.rationale: Zep's first-party Memory MCP Server lets an end user connect MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) to their own agent memory in Zep, so multiple off-the-shelf assistants can share one memory. The open-source Graphiti MCP server, which is experimental, offers a similar path for Claude, Cursor and VS Code Copilot. Sign-in goes through Google Workspace or an enterprise identity provider, which suggests an organization-provisioned setup. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that memory is actually shared across tools, documented setup steps and the tools exposed per client.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect off-the-shelf assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) to the same memory so every tool I use shares what it knows about me

citations.quote: The Memory MCP Server lets an end user connect an MCP client (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others) to their own agent memory in Zep. The user signs in through Google Workspace or your enterprise identity provider.
This enables AI assistants like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code with Copilot to interact with Graphiti's Context Graph capabilities, providing persistent context and contextual awareness.
